title: Valued-field description of admissible-modification stalks
statement:
Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair with $I$ finitely generated, $A'=\widehat A$, $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $U=X\setminus V(I)$, $X'=\operatorname{Spec}A'$ and $U'=X'\times_XU$ [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $F$ be a torsion abelian sheaf on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ and $F'$ its inverse image on $U'_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Use the common limit topos $\mathcal T$ of the closed fibres of the admissible blowups and the sheaves $L^q_F,L^q_{F'}$ defined by the colimits of restricted higher direct images in [lem-per-admissible-modification-cohomology-presentation]. Its geometric points admit a conservative subfamily with the following property. For each point $t$ in that subfamily there are nontrivially valued fields $K_t\hookrightarrow K'_t$, both henselian for their valuation rings [def-trf-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], such that the inclusion induces the valuation topology on $K_t$ and has dense image in $K'_t$. There is a torsion abelian etale sheaf $G_t$ on $\operatorname{Spec}K_t$ and, simultaneously for every $q\geq0$, natural identifications
$$(L^q_F)_t\cong H^q((\operatorname{Spec}K_t)_{\mathrm{et}},G_t),\qquad (L^q_{F'})_t\cong H^q((\operatorname{Spec}K'_t)_{\mathrm{et}},G_t|_{K'_t}).$$
They identify the stalk of the exchange map $L^q_F\to L^q_{F'}$ with the canonical field-extension pullback on these groups [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. A valuation topology has neighbourhoods of zero given by the inequalities $v(x)>\gamma$ in an ordered value group; dense means that each nonempty open ball meets the subfield. No isomorphism on these cohomology groups is asserted.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373--374: paragraph beginning Using the study in Fujiwara, reduction to henselian I-valuative local rings, then to their valued residue fraction fields.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-admissible-modification-fujiwara-valuative-local] to the given pair and sheaf. Retain its conservative family of points, independent of the cohomological degree. For one such point suppress the index $t$ and write $B,C,u,\varphi,\psi$ for its two strict-local colimit rings, their local map and their exceptional equations, with $\psi=u(\varphi)$. The cited statement supplies the nonzero henselian local rings, the nonunit nonzerodivisors, the principal-ideal property in each ring, and, simultaneously for every $q$, the restriction isomorphisms from the two stalks to cohomology on $\operatorname{Spec}S$ and $\operatorname{Spec}T$, where $S=B[1/\varphi]$ and $T=C[1/\psi]$. It also identifies the exchange morphism with pullback along $S\to T$.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.373, paragraph beginning Using the study in Fujiwara: local rings and coefficient stalks.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-admissible-modification-valuative-ring-reduction] separately to $(B,\varphi)$ and $(C,\psi)$; all its hypotheses were supplied in step 1. Put $P=\bigcap_{n\geq1}\varphi^nB$, $Q=\bigcap_{n\geq1}\psi^nC$, $V=B/P$, and $W=C/Q$. Thus $S,T$ are henselian local with maximal ideals $PS,QT$; $V,W$ are henselian valuation rings; and their fraction fields are $K=V[1/\bar\varphi]=S/PS$ and $K'=W[1/\bar\psi]=T/QT$. The images $\bar\varphi,\bar\psi$ are nonzero nonunits, so the valuations are nontrivial. Their positive powers give neighbourhood bases of zero. These are the fields and valuation rings we will use, rather than the rings $S,T$ themselves.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373–374, Say I=(phi), the prime intersection, henselian localization and valuation quotient.

proof.text: The rings and geometric points in step 1 are exactly those in [lem-per-admissible-modification-completion-density], so its congruences give $B/\varphi^nB\simeq C/\psi^nC$ via $u$ for every $n\geq1$. Since $P\subseteq\varphi^nB$ and $Q\subseteq\psi^nC$, these also give $V/\bar\varphi^nV\simeq W/\bar\psi^nW$. Moreover $u(P)\subseteq Q$, and $u(b)\in Q$ implies $b\in\varphi^nB$ for every $n$ by injectivity of these congruences, hence $b\in P$. Therefore $u$ induces an injection $V\hookrightarrow W$, which extends uniquely to a field inclusion $K\hookrightarrow K'$. The maps from $B,C$ and their localizations to these fields commute, by the formulas $b/\varphi^m\mapsto u(b)/\psi^m$ and reduction modulo $P,Q$.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374 final Note: equal infinitesimal closed fibres; elementary passage from the admitted strict-local congruences to separated quotients.

proof.text: The map $V\to W$ is local: their maximal ideals are the images of those of $B,C$, and $u$ is local. For $x\in K\setminus V$, the valuation-ring definition [def-trf-valuation-ring] gives $x^{-1}\in V$; it is a nonunit, since otherwise $x\in V$. Its image is a nonunit of $W$, so $x\notin W$. Consequently $K\cap W=V$. Dividing by $\bar\varphi^n$ in $K$ gives $K\cap\bar\psi^nW=\bar\varphi^nV$ for every $n\geq1$. The neighbourhood bases from step 2 now show exactly that the subspace topology induced from $K'$ is the valuation topology on $K$.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373–374, the phi-adic valuation topology; explicit elementary verification for the local inclusion of valuation rings.

proof.text: To verify density, let $x\in K'$ and $N\geq1$. Write $x=a/\bar\psi^m$ with $a\in W$ and $m\geq0$, using $K'=W[1/\bar\psi]$. The congruence isomorphism of step 3 with exponent $N+m$ supplies $b\in V$ such that $a-u(b)\in\bar\psi^{N+m}W$. Then $y=b/\bar\varphi^m\in K$ satisfies $x-y\in\bar\psi^NW$. These cosets form a neighbourhood basis at every $x$ by step 2, so every nonempty open ball in $K'$ meets $K$.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374, dense embedding of henselian valued fields; explicit approximation using the final Note.

proof.text: Let $i:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ and $i':\operatorname{Spec}K'\to\operatorname{Spec}T$ be the closed-point inclusions from step 2, and put $G=i^{-1}F_t$. All of $F_t,F'_t,G$ are torsion by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-torsion]. Since $S,T$ are henselian local, their pairs with their maximal ideals are henselian by definition. Apply [prop-weil-pbc-gabber-pair-comparison] to these two affine pairs and the two torsion sheaves. The restriction maps give $H^q(S,F_t)\simeq H^q(K,G)$ and $H^q(T,F'_t)\simeq H^q(K',(i')^{-1}F'_t)$ for all $q\geq0$. Composing with step 1 gives the required two stalk identifications. This application is to the spectra of the henselian rings themselves; it requires no finite-type or excellence hypothesis.

source.place: Theorem Tag 09ZI (theorem-gabber), applied to the maximal-ideal henselian pairs; Tag 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback) and section Tag 0DDB (section-torsion) for torsion inverse images.

proof.text: Write $h:\operatorname{Spec}K'\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $f:\operatorname{Spec}T\to\operatorname{Spec}S$. Step 3 gives the equality $f\circ i'=i\circ h$. Since $F'_t=f^{-1}F_t$, the canonical inverse-image composition identifications identify $(i')^{-1}F'_t$ with $h^{-1}G$. Apply the composition clause (4) of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] to the two sides of this square. For every $q$ it says $(i')^*\circ f^*=h^*\circ i^*$ under those coefficient identifications. Step 1 identifies $f^*$ with exchange on stalks, and step 6 identifies $i^*,(i')^*$ with the displayed isomorphisms. Thus exchange becomes precisely $h^*$, the canonical field-extension pullback. Clause (3) gives naturality in $F$. The family, fields, and $G$ were chosen before $q$, so these identifications hold simultaneously in all degrees.

source.place: Tag 01F7 (section-functoriality), Lemma Tag 01F8 (lemma-functoriality), equation Tag 01FA (equation-functorial), and Remark Tag 01FB (remark-explain-arrow); admitted etale pullback interface, clauses (3)–(4).

proof_origin.place: XX 4.4, printed pp.373–374; the local reduction follows its sketch, with explicit elementary density/topology algebra and the admitted Stacks 09ZI and pullback-functoriality tools.
